answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each vote cost locked capital, not just a key pair. At dawn the round opens and every agent posts a bond before its vote counts, so identity is defined by collateral. A comet burst of freshly minted accounts still needs one separate bond each, so the attacker's cost grows linearly with the number of fakes. Caught double-voting, that bond is slashed. Even a plume of forged registrations cannot outweigh honest stake, because weight follows locked funds, not headcount.
